name: Death Valley National Park
about: Unlike most desert parks, winter (Nov–Mar) is the real high season here, while Jun–Aug regularly hits 120°F and hiking is genuinely dangerous.
overview: The hottest place on Earth on record — vast salt flats, badlands, and sand dunes below sea level.
costOverview: Prices stay close to typical national-park levels — Furnace Creek's isolation pushes food costs up slightly, though nothing here reaches resort-town prices.

specialSeasons.text: Daytime highs regularly exceed 120°F and hiking is genuinely dangerous — stick to short, early-morning walks and never hike after 10am if you visit now.
In years with enough winter rain, wildflowers carpet the valley floor in a rare superbloom — timing and intensity vary hugely year to year.
